text: function builds whitened cross-product S = (M_X^{1/2} X W_X^{1/2})' (M_Y^{1/2} Y W_Y^{1/2}) explicitly runs dense SVD. intentionally small dense; package’s operator-based path avoids materialising whitened matrices.
code: make_sqrt_mats <- function(W, n) {   if (is.null(W)) {     list(sqrt = Diagonal(n), invsqrt = Diagonal(n), full = Diagonal(n))   } else if (is.numeric(W) && length(W) == n) {     d  <- pmax(as.numeric(W), 0)     ds <- sqrt(d)     list(sqrt    = Diagonal(x = ds),          invsqrt = Diagonal(x = ifelse(ds > 0, 1 / ds, 0)),          full    = Diagonal(x = d))   } else if (inherits(W, "diagonalMatrix")) {     d  <- pmax(as.numeric(diag(W)), 0)     ds <- sqrt(d)     list(sqrt    = Diagonal(x = ds),          invsqrt = Diagonal(x = ifelse(ds > 0, 1 / ds, 0)),          full    = W)   } else {     Wd  <- as.matrix(forceSymmetric(Matrix(W)))     es  <- eigen(Wd, symmetric = TRUE)     Q   <- es$vectors     lam <- pmax(es$values, 0)     S   <- Q %*% diag(sqrt(lam), nrow = length(lam)) %*% t(Q)     IS  <- Q %*% diag(ifelse(lam > 0, 1 / sqrt(lam), 0), nrow = length(lam)) %*% t(Q)     list(sqrt    = Matrix(S,  sparse = FALSE),          invsqrt = Matrix(IS, sparse = FALSE),          full    = Matrix(Wd, sparse = FALSE))   } }  dense_gplssvd_ref <- function(X, Y,                               MX = NULL, MY = NULL,                               WX = NULL, WY = NULL,                               k = NULL,                               center = FALSE, scale = FALSE) {   N <- nrow(X); I <- ncol(X); J <- ncol(Y)   stopifnot(nrow(Y) == N)    cs <- function(A, do_center, do_scale) {     A   <- as.matrix(A)     cen <- if (isTRUE(do_center)) colMeans(A) else rep(0, ncol(A))     if (isTRUE(do_center)) A <- A - matrix(rep(cen, each = nrow(A)), nrow(A))     if (isTRUE(do_scale)) {       s <- sqrt(colSums(A^2) / pmax(nrow(A) - 1, 1))       s[s == 0] <- 1       A <- A %*% diag(1 / as.numeric(s), ncol(A))     } else s <- rep(1, ncol(A))     list(A = A, center = cen, scale = s)   }    Xcs <- cs(X, center, scale); X <- Xcs$A   Ycs <- cs(Y, center, scale); Y <- Ycs$A    MXm <- make_sqrt_mats(MX, N); MYm <- make_sqrt_mats(MY, N)   WXm <- make_sqrt_mats(WX, I); WYm <- make_sqrt_mats(WY, J)    Xe <- MXm$sqrt %*% X %*% WXm$sqrt   Ye <- MYm$sqrt %*% Y %*% WYm$sqrt   S  <- crossprod(Xe, Ye)    sv <- svd(as.matrix(S))   if (!is.null(k)) {     k     <- min(k, length(sv$d))     sv$u  <- sv$u[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE]     sv$v  <- sv$v[, seq_len(k), drop = FALSE]     sv$d  <- sv$d[seq_len(k)]   }    p  <- WXm$invsqrt %*% sv$u   q  <- WYm$invsqrt %*% sv$v   Fi <- WXm$full %*% (p %*% diag(sv$d, nrow = length(sv$d)))   Fj <- WYm$full %*% (q %*% diag(sv$d, nrow = length(sv$d)))   Lx <- MXm$sqrt %*% (X %*% (WXm$full %*% p))   Ly <- MYm$sqrt %*% (Y %*% (WYm$full %*% q))    list(d = sv$d, u = sv$u, v = sv$v, p = p, q = q,        fi = Fi, fj = Fj, lx = Lx, ly = Ly, S = S,        center = list(X = Xcs$center, Y = Ycs$center),        scale  = list(X = Xcs$scale,  Y = Ycs$scale)) }

title: Generalized Principal Component Analysis
text: Standard PCA assumes observations variables equally important Euclidean distance appropriate similarity measure. However, many real-world datasets violate assumptions: Weighted observations: Survey data rows represent different population sizes Variable precision: Measurements different accuracies importance Correlated features: Spatial/temporal data known dependency structures Domain-specific geometry: Functional data, shape analysis, specialized metrics GPCA extends standard PCA incorporating row column metrics (M ) encode prior knowledge data structure, following framework Allen, Grosenick & Taylor (2014). package also implements generalized PLS methods building ideas Beaton et al. (2016).

text: X Numeric matrix n x p. Column constraint: vector (implies diagonal), dense matrix, sparse symmetric p x p PSD matrix. NULL, defaults identity. M Row constraint: vector (implies diagonal), dense matrix, sparse symmetric n x n PSD matrix. NULL, defaults identity. ncomp Number components extract. Defaults min(dim(X)). Must positive. method Character string specifying computation method. One "eigen" (default, uses gmdLA), "auto" (heuristic choice among "eigen", "spectra", "randomized"), "spectra" (uses matrix-free C++/Spectra implementation gmd_fast_cpp), "randomized" (approximate randomized block solver gmd_randomized), "deflation" (uses gmd_deflationR gmd_deflation_cpp). constraints_remedy Character string specifying supplied M symmetric positive (semi)definite repaired. Default "ridge". One : "error" (reject input error), "ridge" (Gershgorin diagonal shift: add smallest diagonal loading restores positive definiteness, falling back Matrix::nearPD() small dense matrices), "clip" (spectral clip PSD cone zeroing negative eigenvalues; densifies matrix refuses sparse input larger 2000 rows/cols, "ridge" used instead), "identity" (replace matrix identity). title: genpca 0.1.0
text: Initial CRAN submission. Generalized PCA row metric M column metric (genpca()), following Allen, Grosenick & Taylor (2014). Covariance-based GPCA precomputed C = X' M X (genpca_cov()), eigen gmd paths. Multiple computational backends: eigen, spectra (matrix-free C++ via RSpectra), randomized, deflation. auto heuristic picks among . Generalized PLS / PLS-SVD two blocks (genpls(), genplsc()) operator-level interface (gplssvd_op()) avoids materialising whitened matrices. Sparse functional PCA (sfpca()), regularised PLS (rpls()), matrix-normal PCA via maximum residual likelihood (mnpca_mrl()). sfpca() solves rank-1 subproblem exactly via C++ coordinate descent constraint form Allen & Weylandt (2019), deflates implicitly (sparse inputs never densify), selects sparsity penalties per component BIC along warm-started lambda path; smoothness weights default scale-free 1 / lambda_max(Omega). former uthresh/vthresh quantile heuristics deprecated. sfpca() now returns multivarious bi_projector (class "sfpca"), scores(), components(), sdev(), reconstruct() work genpca(). pre-0.1 list fields $d $u remain readable emit deprecation warning. Maximum-likelihood metric learning (gpca_mle()). SPD constraint handling "ridge", "clip", "identity" remediation strategies. Vignettes covering getting started, metric recipes, scaling, reference implementation GPLSSVD.

title: genpca 0.1.0
text: gpca_mle() now optimizes single penalized (MAP) matrix-normal objective exact block updates (sequential flip-flop covariance updates; ridge lambda part objective), loglik_path monotone non-decreasing. scale_fix applied exit joint, likelihood-preserving rescale (row covariance normalized, factor absorbed column covariance) instead normalizing factors independently iteration, returned fit computed returned canonicalized metrics. Reported log-likelihood values now include penalty term, differ numerically previous versions. scores() genpca fits now matches Allen, Grosenick & Taylor (2014)’s convention (z_k = X ov_k = ou_k d_k) identical project(fit, X) training data; previously two disagree. reconstruct.genpca(fit, colind = ) now applies inverse pre-processing transform selected columns, rather first length(colind) columns. Deflation convergence degeneracy thresholds (threshold argument genpca(method = "deflation") internal SFPCA solver) now relative scale problem rather absolute, results invariant rescaling input data. constraints_remedy = "clip" now performs real spectral clip PSD cone (previously clip); requires dense eigendecomposition refuses sparse input larger 2000 rows/columns, recommending "ridge" instead. Fixed PSD validation dense (non-diagonal) constraint matrices indefinite input reliably rejected/repaired rather silently accepted. genpca(method = "randomized") longer mutates caller’s .Random.seed; C++ kernel seeds stream seed_randomized, now fully controls reproducibility. Added input validation (dimensions, finiteness, penalty/scad_a range, strictly positive diagonal) internal C++ coordinate-descent solver used sfpca(). Fixed cache-key collision internal matrix-decomposition cache: digest previously used rounded matrix entries, collide distinct matrices (e.g. metric ridge-remediated version) return wrong cached factor; digest now hashes exact bytes. genpls()’s $ncomp field now reports number components actually extracted, may less requested ncomp.
